label: Threat intelligence bulletin
text:
THREAT BULLETIN TB-2026-0917 | Regional Cyber Coordination Centre (fictional sample)

Ransomware group "Ember Spider" actively exploiting SecureGate VPN vulnerability CVE-2026-31742

Summary
Since 9 September 2026, the ransomware affiliate group tracked as Ember Spider has been exploiting a critical authentication-bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-31742 (CVSS 9.8), in SecureGate VPN appliances running firmware versions 7.2.0 through 7.4.3. The flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an administrative session by sending a crafted request to the /remote/saml/login endpoint. The vendor released fixed firmware 7.4.4 on 12 September 2026.

Observed activity
The Centre has confirmed intrusions at 14 organisations across banking, healthcare and logistics in India and Southeast Asia. After gaining VPN access, the actors create a local administrator account, disable endpoint protection using a signed but vulnerable driver, and move laterally with RDP and PsExec. Data is staged and exfiltrated to cloud storage using Rclone before encryption begins. The median time from initial access to encryption has been 3.5 days, giving defenders a narrow but real window to detect and evict the intruders.

Ransom demands have ranged from USD 1.2 million to USD 4.5 million. Victims receive a note titled README_EMBER.txt and are threatened with publication of stolen data on a leak site within 7 days.

Exposure
Internet scanning by the Centre identified approximately 41,000 SecureGate appliances exposed to the internet in the region. As of 25 September 2026, an estimated 38% of them still run a vulnerable firmware version.

Indicators of compromise
- Source IPs: 203.0.113.45, 198.51.100.23
- Domain: update-securegate[.]net
- File: svcupd.exe (SHA-256 begins 9f2c41ab)
- Local account names created: sg_support, vpnadmin2

Recommended actions
Organisations using SecureGate VPN should upgrade to firmware 7.4.4 immediately. Where patching is not possible within 24 hours, disable SAML login on the appliance. Review appliance logs since 1 September 2026 for requests to /remote/saml/login and for new local accounts. Reset credentials for all VPN and domain administrator accounts, enforce phishing-resistant MFA, and block the listed indicators. Report confirmed incidents to the Centre within 6 hours of detection.

video.title: Patch Before Day Four: The Ember Spider VPN Campaign
video.logline: A 60-second alert showing how one VPN flaw opened the door to 14 ransomware intrusions, and the three things every team must do today.

video.script:
SCENE 1 - The Open Door
One unpatched VPN appliance. That is all Ember Spider needs.

SCENE 2 - The Flaw
CVE-2026-31742 lets an attacker skip the login entirely and walk in as an administrator. It carries a severity score of 9.8 out of 10.

SCENE 3 - The Campaign
Since 9 September, 14 organisations in banking, healthcare and logistics have been breached. Data is stolen first, then encrypted, with ransom demands up to 4.5 million dollars.

SCENE 4 - The Clock
From first access to encryption takes a median of just 3.5 days. And 38 percent of exposed devices are still unpatched.

SCENE 5 - What To Do Now
Upgrade to firmware 7.4.4 today. Can't patch in 24 hours? Disable SAML login. Then hunt: check logs, reset admin credentials, block the indicators.

SCENE 6 - Close
Report confirmed incidents within 6 hours. Patch before day four.

3.5 days. That is the median time Ember Spider needs to go from your VPN login page to encrypted servers.

Since 9 September 2026, this ransomware group has been exploiting CVE-2026-31742, a critical authentication bypass (CVSS 9.8) in SecureGate VPN firmware 7.2.0 to 7.4.3.

What we know so far:
→ 14 organisations breached across banking, healthcare and logistics
→ Data is exfiltrated with Rclone before anything is encrypted
→ Ransom demands of USD 1.2 million to USD 4.5 million
→ Around 41,000 appliances are exposed, and 38% were still unpatched on 25 September

The fix exists. Firmware 7.4.4 was released on 12 September.

If you run SecureGate VPN, three things for today:
1. Upgrade to 7.4.4. If you cannot within 24 hours, disable SAML login.
2. Review logs since 1 September for requests to /remote/saml/login and new local admin accounts.
3. Reset VPN and domain admin credentials and enforce phishing-resistant MFA.

Patching is the cheapest incident response you will ever do.

Security leaders: where does VPN firmware sit in your patch SLA today?

advisory.title: Active exploitation of SecureGate VPN CVE-2026-31742 by Ember Spider ransomware
advisory.summary: Ember Spider, a ransomware affiliate group, is exploiting CVE-2026-31742 (CVSS 9.8), an authentication bypass in SecureGate VPN firmware 7.2.0 to 7.4.3, to gain administrative access. At least 14 organisations have been compromised since 9 September 2026. Fixed firmware 7.4.4 is available and must be applied immediately.
advisory.background: SecureGate VPN appliances provide remote access for a large share of regional enterprises. A flaw in the SAML login endpoint (/remote/saml/login) lets a crafted request return an administrative session without credentials. The vendor released firmware 7.4.4 on 12 September 2026.
affected: SecureGate VPN appliances on firmware 7.2.0 through 7.4.3
Banking, healthcare and logistics organisations in India and Southeast Asia (confirmed victims)
Any organisation with an internet-exposed SecureGate management or SAML endpoint
advisory.impact: Full administrative control of the VPN appliance, followed by domain-wide lateral movement, data theft and ransomware encryption within a median of 3.5 days. Stolen data is threatened with publication within 7 days, creating regulatory and reputational exposure in addition to operational downtime.

details.heading: Exploitation
details.body: A crafted request to /remote/saml/login returns an administrative session without authentication. Exploitation has been observed since 9 September 2026.

details.heading: Post-exploitation tradecraft
details.body: Actors create local administrator accounts, disable endpoint protection using a signed but vulnerable driver, and move laterally with RDP and PsExec.

details.heading: Exfiltration and extortion
details.body: Data is staged and exfiltrated to cloud storage using Rclone before encryption. Ransom notes are named README_EMBER.txt; demands range from USD 1.2 million to USD 4.5 million.

details.heading: Exposure
details.body: Approximately 41,000 SecureGate appliances are internet-exposed in the region; an estimated 38% remained on vulnerable firmware as of 25 September 2026.

recommendations.action: Upgrade all SecureGate VPN appliances to firmware 7.4.4.
If patching within 24 hours is not possible, disable SAML login on the appliance.
Block the listed IP addresses and domain at the perimeter and on DNS resolvers.
Review appliance logs since 1 September 2026 for requests to /remote/saml/login and creation of local accounts.
Reset credentials for all VPN and domain administrator accounts.
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for remote access and privileged accounts.
Report confirmed incidents to the Centre within 6 hours of detection.

executive_summary.title: Executive Briefing: Ember Spider ransomware campaign via SecureGate VPN
executive_summary.bottom_line: A critical, actively exploited VPN flaw has led to 14 ransomware breaches in three weeks; any SecureGate appliance not on firmware 7.4.4 should be treated as a live incident risk today.
executive_summary.situation: Since 9 September 2026 the Ember Spider group has exploited CVE-2026-31742 (CVSS 9.8) to take administrative control of SecureGate VPN appliances without credentials. Victims in banking, healthcare and logistics have had data stolen and systems encrypted, with ransom demands of USD 1.2 million to USD 4.5 million.
key_findings: The flaw affects SecureGate VPN firmware 7.2.0 through 7.4.3; version 7.4.4 fixes it.
14 organisations in India and Southeast Asia are confirmed compromised.
Attackers reach encryption in a median of 3.5 days, after stealing data first.
About 38% of roughly 41,000 exposed appliances remained unpatched on 25 September 2026.
implications: If we run an unpatched appliance, we should assume compromise is possible and verify, not just patch.
Data theft before encryption means regulatory notification and reputational exposure even if backups are intact.
The 6-hour reporting expectation requires incident response to be on standby.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm SecureGate inventory and upgrade every appliance to firmware 7.4.4.
Disable SAML login on any appliance that cannot be patched immediately.
Run a compromise assessment on logs since 1 September 2026 and reset admin credentials.
Mandate phishing-resistant MFA for remote and privileged access.

risks: Patching alone does not evict an attacker who already has access.
Leak-site publication within 7 days of an incident could trigger customer and regulator scrutiny.
executive_summary.decision_required: Approve an emergency change window today for VPN firmware upgrades and authorise a compromise assessment.

presentation.title: Ember Spider & CVE-2026-31742
presentation.subtitle: Threat briefing for leadership and security teams

slides.title: Ember Spider & CVE-2026-31742
slides.visual_suggestion: Dark cover with a faint VPN appliance silhouette
slides.speaker_notes: Good morning. This briefing covers an active ransomware campaign exploiting a critical flaw in SecureGate VPN appliances. I will cover what is happening, how exposed we are as a region, and the three decisions we need today. Everything I present comes from Threat Bulletin TB-2026-0917 issued by the Regional Cyber Coordination Centre.

slides.title: What is happening
bullets: Ember Spider exploiting CVE-2026-31742 since 9 September 2026
Authentication bypass: admin session without credentials
slides.speaker_notes: The core problem is simple. A crafted request to the SAML login page gives an attacker an administrative session without any password. Ember Spider started using this on 9 September. The vendor shipped a fix three days later in firmware 7.4.4, so this is a patching race, not a zero-day with no answer.

slides.title: Organisations already breached
slides.stat_label: across banking, healthcare and logistics in India and Southeast Asia
slides.speaker_notes: Fourteen organisations are confirmed compromised so far. They are in banking, healthcare and logistics, sectors where downtime and data exposure are both very costly. We should expect this number to grow while so many appliances remain unpatched.

slides.title: Attack chain and exposure
bullets: Disable EDR with a vulnerable signed driver
Move laterally via RDP and PsExec
slides.visual_suggestion: Left: attack chain arrows. Right: exposure numbers
slides.speaker_notes: On the left is the attack chain. After getting in, they create admin accounts, switch off endpoint protection and spread across the network before stealing data and encrypting. On the right is why this matters: tens of thousands of devices are exposed and more than a third were still vulnerable last week. Our window to detect an intrusion is roughly three and a half days.

slides.title: Actions for today
bullets: Cannot patch in 24h: disable SAML login
Reset VPN and domain admin credentials
Block listed IPs, domain and accounts
slides.speaker_notes: These are the actions the bulletin asks for. Patch first. If a device cannot be patched within a day, turn off SAML login as a stop-gap. Then assume we might already have been touched: review logs, look for the two known account names, reset admin passwords and block the indicators. The SOC has the indicator list.

slides.title: Reporting obligation
slides.quote: Report confirmed incidents to the Centre within 6 hours of detection.
slides.speaker_notes: One more requirement to be aware of: confirmed incidents must be reported to the Centre within six hours. That means our incident response lead needs to be on standby and the escalation path must be clear before anything happens, not after.

slides.title: Longer-term hardening
bullets: Phishing-resistant MFA for remote and privileged access
VPN firmware inside a critical-patch SLA of days, not weeks
Continuous monitoring of edge appliance logs
slides.visual_suggestion: Roadmap strip: now, next month, next quarter
slides.speaker_notes: Beyond this incident, the lesson is that edge devices like VPNs are a favourite entry point. Phishing-resistant MFA is directly recommended in the bulletin. The other two items are my recommendations to make sure the next critical VPN flaw gets patched in hours, not weeks.

slides.title: Decisions needed today
slides.speaker_notes: To close, I need three decisions: an emergency change window for the firmware upgrade, approval for a compromise assessment on our appliances, and confirmation that incident response is on standby for the six-hour reporting window. Happy to take questions.
